title: California State Workers Announce Statewide One-Day Strike

tea.why: Protesting alleged bad-faith bargaining practices by the state administration during labor contract negotiations.
tea.want: Demanding a 20% wage increase over three years, flexible telework options, in-office stipends, and increased healthcare contributions.
tea.changed: Oct 7: The union called for a one-day statewide strike following stalled negotiations and a 96.2% authorization vote.

summary: Tens of thousands of California state government workers represented by SEIU Local 1000 announced a one-day statewide walkout. Organised following the expiration of their three-year labor contract on June 30, the strike stems from accusations that Governor Gavin Newsom’s administration engaged in bad-faith bargaining practices, including the rejection of multiple union proposals. The union seeks wage increases totaling roughly 20% over three years, telework flexibility, in-office stipends, and higher state healthcare contributions. The action is expected to affect public services across various agencies, including the DMV, unemployment offices, and state parks. State officials previously sought a temporary restraining order to halt the walkout through the Public Employment Relations Board, but the request was rejected.
demands: Wage increases of about 20% across three years
Stipends for workers required to be in the office
Increased state contributions toward healthcare costs
response: According to the sources, the state asked the Public Employment Relations Board to issue a temporary restraining order to stop the strike, arguing mediations should finish first, but PERB rejected the request.

updates.text: SEIU Local 1000 officially called for a one-day statewide strike after a 96.2% approval vote by members.
